description: This line plot illustrates the relative change in performance (likely model accuracy or a similar metric) across different transformer model layers when applying various key-value (KV) cache compression strategies, compared to a baseline. The x-axis represents the model’s layer groups: “Layer1-4”, “Layer5-12”, “Layer13-20”, “Layer21-28”, and “Layer29-32”, indicating a grouped, categorical scale. The y-axis, labeled “Relative Change”, is a linear scale ranging from approximately -20% to +5%, with major gridlines at 5% intervals, showing how much each compression method deviates from the baseline. Five distinct lines are plotted: the gray dashed line for the “Baseline of 4×tokens,4-bit” remains flat at 0% across all layers, serving as the reference. The yellow line with circle markers (“LB-Avg of 2×tokens,8-bit”) starts near 0%, dips slightly to about -2% at Layer5-12, then recovers to near 0% by Layer29-32. The red line with square markers (“LB-Avg of 1×tokens,16-bit”) begins near 0%, drops to about -5% at Layer13-20, then rises to about -1% at Layer29-32. The light blue line with circle markers (“RULER4k of 2×tokens,8-bit”) starts at about -2%, drops to -13% at Layer13-20, then recovers to about -2% at Layer29-32. The dark blue line with square markers (“RULER4k of 1×tokens,16-bit”) shows the largest deviation, starting at about -4%, plunging to nearly -20% at Layer13-20, then partially recovering to about -4% at Layer29-32. All lines exhibit a pronounced dip in relative performance around the middle layers (Layer13-20), with varying degrees of recovery in later layers.
